problem.headline: Faults were found by occupants, not by engineers
problem.detail: Across the managed estate, HVAC plant drifted out of tune between annual commissioning visits. A stuck damper or an overridden setpoint went unnoticed until someone complained about a cold floor, by which point the plant had been burning energy against itself for weeks. Engineers spent their time reacting to tickets rather than tuning buildings.

capability.headline: Every building is now commissioned continuously, not annually
capability.detail: Telemetry from the building management systems is read against expected operating envelopes, so simultaneous heating and cooling, stuck actuators and stale overrides surface as ranked findings with a recommended correction. Engineers open a morning queue of what actually needs attention instead of a list of what someone reported.

outcome.headline: Buildings now tell us they are wrong before anyone feels it

significance.headline: One engineer now covers what a team of engineers used to walk
significance.detail: The same detection service runs against any site whose plant is already instrumented, so adding a building to the programme is a configuration change rather than a new engagement. Energy performance stops decaying between visits, which is what makes the savings hold rather than appear once and erode.

claims.metric: time to detect a plant fault
reactive callouts per building per year

assumption.statement: assumes the pilot estate's fault profile is representative of the wider portfolio, and that callout volume scales with detected faults rather than with occupancy

claims.statement: Every setpoint change now carries the finding that prompted it, the engineer who accepted it, and a one-click reversal path
